---
title: "Why has the aspect ratio been driven so low?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
# Aspect ratio held at each point with the other three variables re-optimised
# around it, so a swept design is never judged against rivals that were not
# allowed to adapt to it.
ARS = [2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 8.0, 10.0, 12.0]
sweep = [optimise(static_margin=0.10, hold={"aspect_ratio": ar}) for ar in ARS]

lo, hi = sweep[0], sweep[-1]
best = min(sweep, key=lambda r: r["sink"])
prof_share = best["CDp"] / (best["CDp"] + best["CDi"])
flat = [r for r in sweep if r["sink"] < 1.02 * best["sink"]]

assert best["CDp"] > best["CDi"]  # the section, not the span, is the cost
assert hi["CDp"] > lo["CDp"] and hi["CDi"] < lo["CDi"]  # the two terms oppose
assert hi["mass"] < lo["mass"]  # low AR is the HEAVIER choice, and still wins
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{prof_share:.0%}"`]{.hero-value}
[of the drag at the optimum is the section, not the wingspan]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Span is fixed, so chord is the only lever on thickness ratio, and
5 mm stock on a `{python} f"{hi['chord']*1e3:.0f}"` mm chord is a
[`{python} f"{hi['tc']:.0%}"`]{.key} slab. Across the sweep profile drag rises
`{python} f"{hi['CDp']/lo['CDp']:.1f}"`× while induced drag falls
`{python} f"{lo['CDi']/hi['CDi']:.0f}"`× (@fig-ar, @tbl-ar). Low aspect ratio is
also the heavier choice, by [`{python} f"{lo['mass']/hi['mass']:.1f}"`×]{.key},
and still wins.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A fact about the foam, not about gliders
Thinner stock would move this more than any reshaping.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Static margin 10%** at every swept point.
2. **One start per solve**; the surface has several basins.
3. **Aspect ratio confined to `{python} f"{DESIGN_BOUNDS['aspect_ratio']}"`.**
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-ar
#| fig-cap: "Left: the two drag components against aspect ratio, each at its own re-optimised design. Right: the resulting sink rate, with the swept minimum marked and the band within 2% of it shaded. Aspect ratio is on a log scale."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.0, 2.7))

ax1.plot(ARS, [r["CDp"] for r in sweep], "o-", ms=4, label="profile")
ax1.plot(ARS, [r["CDi"] for r in sweep], "s-", ms=4, label="induced")
ax1.set_ylabel("drag coefficient")
ax1.legend()

ax2.plot(ARS, [r["sink"] for r in sweep], "o-", ms=4, color="C2")
ax2.axvspan(min(r["aspect_ratio"] for r in flat),
            max(r["aspect_ratio"] for r in flat), color="C0", alpha=0.12)
ax2.plot(best["aspect_ratio"], best["sink"], "o", ms=8, color="C0")
ax2.set_ylabel("sink rate, m/s")

for ax in (ax1, ax2):
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_xticks(ARS, [f"{a:g}" for a in ARS])
    ax.minorticks_off()
    ax.set_xlabel("aspect ratio")
    ax.grid()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ar
#| tbl-cap: "The swept designs. Chord, thickness ratio and Reynolds number are consequences of aspect ratio at fixed span; mass, the two drag components and sink are results of the solve at each point."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print("| AR | chord, mm | t/c | Re | mass, g | CD profile | CD induced | sink, m/s |")
print("|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
for r in sweep:
    print(f"| {r['aspect_ratio']:.1f} | {r['chord']*1e3:.0f} | {r['tc']:.1%} "
          f"| {r['Re']:.0f} | {r['mass']*1e3:.2f} | {r['CDp']:.4f} "
          f"| {r['CDi']:.4f} | {r['sink']:.3f} |")
```
